Bots got popular, and some members create far too many of them:

> As an administrator, I want to cap how many bots each member can have.

The account settings page (`/account/edit`) gets a new setting for administrators:

- "Bots per member" (a number, 5 by default)

Rules:

- A member can have at most that many bots. Deleted bots don't count.
- Administrators are not limited.
- At the limit, the bots page doesn't offer "Add a chat bot" and tells the member they've "reached the limit". Any other attempt to create a bot is refused, too.
- Lowering the limit never removes existing bots; it only blocks new ones.

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Avatar, Bannable, Bot, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  validates :name, presence: true

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms_on_create
  after_update_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms_on_update

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }
  scope :auto_joining_open_rooms, -> { where.not(role: :bot).or(where(role: :bot, add_to_all_open_rooms: true)) }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def auto_joins_open_rooms?
    !bot? || add_to_all_open_rooms?
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all
      webhook&.destroy!

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address, bot_token: nil
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms_on_create
      grant_membership_to_open_rooms if active? && auto_joins_open_rooms?
    end

    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms_on_update
      grant_membership_to_open_rooms if active? && bot? && saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true)
    end

    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      records = Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } }
      Membership.grant_records(records)
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end

module User::Bot
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true
    has_one :webhook, dependent: :destroy

    before_validation :initialize_bot, on: :create, if: :bot?
    validate :validate_webhook_url, if: :bot?
    after_save :sync_webhook, if: :bot?

    scope :without_bots, -> { where.not(role: :bot) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def create_bot!(attributes)
      create! attributes.merge(role: :bot)
    end

    def authenticate_bot(bot_key)
      id, token = bot_key.to_s.split("-", 2)
      return nil unless id&.match?(/\A\d+\z/) && token.present?

      if bot = active.bot.find_by(id: id)
        bot if bot.bot_token.present? && ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(bot.bot_token, token)
      end
    end
  end

  def bot_key
    "#{id}-#{bot_token}" if bot? && bot_token.present?
  end

  def webhook_url
    if defined?(@webhook_url)
      @webhook_url
    else
      webhook&.url
    end
  end

  def webhook_url=(value)
    @webhook_url = value.to_s.strip
  end

  def reload(*)
    remove_instance_variable(:@webhook_url) if defined?(@webhook_url)
    super
  end

  private
    def initialize_bot
      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token
      self.password_digest ||= ""
    end

    def generate_bot_token
      SecureRandom.base58(24)
    end

    def validate_webhook_url
      return unless defined?(@webhook_url) && @webhook_url.present?

      unless Webhook.valid_url?(@webhook_url)
        errors.add :webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL"
      end
    end

    def sync_webhook
      return unless defined?(@webhook_url)

      if @webhook_url.present?
        if webhook
          webhook.update!(url: @webhook_url)
        else
          create_webhook!(url: @webhook_url)
        end
      else
        webhook&.destroy!
        association(:webhook).reset
      end

      remove_instance_variable(:@webhook_url)
    end
end

  require "active_support/core_ext/hash/reverse_merge"
  require "active_support/core_ext/symbol/starts_ends_with"

  module ActiveModel
    module SchematizedJson
      extend ActiveSupport::Concern

      module ClassMethods
        # Provides a schema-enforced access object for a JSON attribute. This allows you to assign values
        # directly from the UI as strings, and still have them set with the correct JSON type in the database.
        #
        # Only the three basic JSON types are supported: boolean, integer, and string. No nesting either.
        # These types can either be set by referring to them by their symbol or by setting a default value.
        # Default values are set when a new model is instantiated and on +before_save+ (if defined).
        def has_json(attr, **schema)
          define_method(attr) do
            # Ensure the attribute is set if nil, so we can pass the reference to the accessor for defaults.
            _write_attribute(attr.to_s, {}) if attribute(attr.to_s).nil?

            # No memoization used in order to stay compatible with #reload (and because it's such a thin accessor).
            ActiveModel::SchematizedJson::DataAccessor.new(schema, data: attribute(attr.to_s))
          end

          define_method("#{attr}=") { |data| public_send(attr).assign_data_with_type_casting(data) }

          # Ensure default values are set before saving by relying on DataAccessor instantiation to do it.
          before_save -> { send(attr) } if respond_to?(:before_save)
        end

        # Like +has_json+ but each schema key also becomes its own set of accessor methods.
        def has_delegated_json(attr, **schema)
          has_json attr, **schema

          schema.keys.each do |schema_key|
            define_method(schema_key)       { public_send(attr).public_send(schema_key) }
            define_method("#{schema_key}?") { public_send(attr).public_send("#{schema_key}?") }
            define_method("#{schema_key}=") { |value| send(attr).public_send("#{schema_key}=", value) }
          end
        end
      end

      # :nodoc:
      class DataAccessor
        def initialize(schema, data:)
          @schema, @data = schema, data
          update_data_with_schema_defaults
        end

        def assign_data_with_type_casting(new_data)
          new_data.each { |k, v| public_send "#{k}=", v }
        end

        private
          def method_missing(method_name, *args, **kwargs)
            key = method_name.to_s.remove(/(\?|=)/)

            if @schema.key? key.to_sym
              if method_name.ends_with?("?")
                @data[key].present?
              elsif method_name.ends_with?("=")
                @data[key] = lookup_schema_type_for(key).cast(args.first)
              else
                @data[key]
              end
            else
              super
            end
          end

          def respond_to_missing?(method_name, include_private = false)
            @schema.key?(method_name.to_s.remove(/[?=]/).to_sym) || super
          end

          def lookup_schema_type_for(key)
            type_or_default_value = @schema[key.to_sym]

            case type_or_default_value
            when :boolean, :integer, :string

            when TrueClass, FalseClass

          # Types that are declared using symbols, like :boolean, :integer, :string, will be nulled out.

class RoomsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ destroy ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show

  def index
    redirect_to room_url(Current.user.rooms.last)
  end

  def show
    @messages = find_messages
  end

  def destroy
    @room.destroy

    broadcast_remove_room
    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_room
      if room = room_scope.find_by(id: params[:room_id] || params[:id])
        @room = room
      else
        redirect_to root_url, alert: "Room not found or inaccessible"
      end
    end

    # Subclasses narrow this to the room types they're allowed to act on, so that one
    # room namespace can't be used to reach another's rooms.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@room)
    end

    def ensure_permission_to_create_rooms
      if Current.account.settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators? && !Current.user.administrator?
        head :forbidden
      end
    end

    def find_messages
      messages = @room.messages.with_creator.with_attachment_details.with_boosts

      if show_first_message = messages.find_by(id: params[:message_id])
        @messages = messages.page_around(show_first_message)
      else
        @messages = messages.last_page
      end
    end

    def room_params
      params.require(:room).permit(:name)
    end

    def broadcast_remove_room
      broadcast_remove_to :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ]
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot sets role, generates unique bot_token and bot_key, and does not join open rooms by default" do
    bot = nil
    assert_no_difference -> { Membership.count } do
      bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    end

    assert bot.bot?
    assert bot.active?
    assert_not bot.add_to_all_open_rooms?
    assert_equal users(:kevin), bot.creator
    assert_equal "", bot.password_digest
    assert_nil bot.email_address
    assert_match /\A[A-Za-z0-9]{24}\z/, bot.bot_token
    assert_equal "#{bot.id}-#{bot.bot_token}", bot.bot_key
    assert_empty bot.rooms

    other_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "CI Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not_equal bot.bot_token, other_bot.bot_token
    assert_not_equal bot.bot_key, other_bot.bot_key
  end

  test "creating a bot with add_to_all_open_rooms joins all existing open rooms" do
    bot = nil
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +Rooms::Open.count do
      bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Everyone Bot", creator: users(:kevin), add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    end

    assert bot.add_to_all_open_rooms?
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
  end

  test "toggling add_to_all_open_rooms on joins missing open rooms and toggling off keeps current memberships" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Toggle Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    rooms(:hq).memberships.grant_to(bot)
    rooms(:watercooler).memberships.grant_to(bot)

    assert_equal [ rooms(:hq).id, rooms(:watercooler).id ].sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort

    # Turning on adds missing open rooms without duplicating existing memberships
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +(Rooms::Open.count - 1) do
      bot.update!(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    end
    assert_equal (Rooms::Open.pluck(:id) + [ rooms(:watercooler).id ]).sort, bot.reload.rooms.pluck(:id).sort

    # Turning off keeps all existing memberships
    assert_no_difference -> { Membership.count } do
      bot.update!(add_to_all_open_rooms: false)
    end
    assert_equal (Rooms::Open.pluck(:id) + [ rooms(:watercooler).id ]).sort, bot.reload.rooms.pluck(:id).sort

    # New open rooms created while off do not include the bot
    later_open = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later Open", creator: users(:david))
    assert_not_includes later_open.users, bot

    # Turning back on joins the newly created open room
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +1 do
      bot.update!(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    end
    assert_includes later_open.reload.users, bot
  end

  test "bot name is required" do
    bot = User.new(role: :bot, name: "   ", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.webhook.url
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.webhook_url

    original_webhook_id = bot.webhook.id

    # Updating name without webhook_url preserves existing webhook

    assert_equal original_webhook_id, bot.relo",

class Rooms::ClosedsController < RoomsController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show edit update ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ update ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show
  before_action :force_room_type, only: %i[ edit update ]
  before_action :ensure_permission_to_create_rooms, only: %i[ new create ]

  DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME = "New room"

  def show
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  def new
    @room  = Rooms::Closed.new(name: DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME)
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Closed.create_for(room_params, users: grantees)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
    selected_user_ids = @room.users.pluck(:id)
    @selected_users, @unselected_users = User.active.ordered.partition { |user| selected_user_ids.include?(user.id) }
  end

  def update
    @room.update! room_params
    @room.memberships.revise(granted: grantees, revoked: revokees)

    broadcast_update_room
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  private
    # Allows us to edit an open room and turn it into a closed one on saving.
    def force_room_type
      @room = @room.becomes!(Rooms::Closed)
    end

    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other, so both are in reach here. Direct
    # rooms never are: converting one would let its creator revise who's in it.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.without_directs
    end

    def grantees
      User.where(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def revokees
      @room.users.where.not(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def grantee_ids
      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      each_user_and_html_for(room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_prepend_to user, :rooms, target: :shared_rooms, html: html
      end
    end

    def broadcast_update_room
      each_user_and_html_for(@room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_replace_to user, :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ], html: html
      end
    end

    def each_user_and_html_for(room)
      # Optimization to avoid rendering the same partial for every user
      html = render_to_string(partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: room })

      room.users.each { |user| yield user, html }
    end
end

    selected_user_ids = @room.users.pluck(:id)
    @selected_users, @unselected_users = User.active.ordered.partition { |user| selected_user_ids.include?(user.id) }
  end

  def update
    @room.update! room_params
    @room.memberships.revise(granted: grantees, revoked: revokees)

    broadcast_update_room
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  private
    # Allows us to edit an open room and turn it into a closed one on saving.
    def force_room_type
      @room = @room.becomes!(Rooms::Closed)
    end

    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other, so both are in reach here. Direct
    # rooms never are: converting one would let its creator revise who's in it.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.without_directs
    end

    def grantees
      User.where(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def revokees
      @room.users.where.not(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def grantee_ids
      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      each_user_and_html_for(room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_prepend_to user, :rooms, target: :shared_rooms, html: html
      end
    end

    def broadcast_update_room
      each_user_and_html_for(@room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_replace_to user, :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ], html: html
      end
    end

    def each_user_and_html_for(room)
      # Optimization to avoid rendering the same partial for every user
      html = render_to_string(partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: room })

      room.users.each { |user| yield user, html }
    end
end

        room: { name: "Ops Team" },
        user_ids: [ users(:david).id, users(:kevin).id, bot.id, other_bot.id ]
      }

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: [ Webhook::DeliveryJob ] do
      put rooms_closed_url(room), params: {
        room: { name: "Ops Team" },
        user_ids: [ users(:david).id, users(:kevin).id, other_bot.id ]
      }
    end
  end

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      records = Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } }
      Membership.grant_records(records)
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

    def deliver_webhooks_later(message)
      message.deliver_webhooks_later
    end

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      records = Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } }
      Membership.grant_records(records)
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

    def deliver_webhooks_later(message)
      message.deliver_webhooks_later
    end
end

module User::Bannable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def ban
    transaction do
      create_bans_from_sessions
      apply_ban
      banned!
    end
  end

  def unban
    transaction do
      bans.delete_all
      active!
    end
  end

  def remove_banned_content_later
    RemoveBannedContentJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def remove_banned_content
    messages.each do |message|
      message.destroy
      message.broadcast_remove
    end
  end

  private
    def create_bans_from_sessions
      sessions.pluck(:ip_address).compact_blank.uniq.each do |ip|
        bans.create!(ip_address: ip)
      end
    end

    def apply_ban
      close_remote_connections
      sessions.delete_all
      remove_banned_content_later
    end
end

messages.thinking:
**Architectural Deep Dive: Model vs. Controller Validation for Bot Limit**

Okay, so I'm seeing a pattern here, and it's making me think. We have this `Room` model with a validation in the model (`validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type`) and a permission check in the controller (`ensure_permission_to_create_rooms`). Now, we need to think about this `User::Bot` situation. The question is, where do we enforce the bot creation limit? Just in the `BotsController`, or also with model validation on `:create`, or BOTH?

Let's break this down meticulously. First, that test in `test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb` – the one that creates 30 bots. Why is it doing that? Is it testing the bot limit explicitly, or is it trying to verify the administrator's ability to see all active bots *regardless* of the limit? I suspect the latter, but the former is now something we need to consider explicitly. I also note that the bot and webhook features were already built, so the test has been inherited.

If we add a model-level validation (`validate :validate_bot_limit, on: :create, if: :bot?`), that existing test will fail unless we update it. We'd have to either temporarily raise the bot limit in the test setup or use an administrator account for bot creation. The question is: *should* we change the test, or avoid the need to change it?

Remember, our QA auto-tests are browser-driven. How would a browser test verify that "Any other attempt to create a bot is refused, too."? It would have to test direct POST requests to `/bots` as well as the `/bots/new` route.

Now, the real software engineering question: Do we validate at the model level, or only in the controller, or both?

Here's my analysis:
**Pros of BOTH (model and controller) validation:**

*   **Defense in Depth:** This is critical. The controller validation handles the normal user interface flow. The model validation provides a safety net if a bot is created through some other route (e.g., console, future API endpoint, background job, model test). It ensures that the rule "A member can have at most that many bots" is *always* enforced, no matter how the bot is created.
*   **Existing Tests:** This raises the need to update existing tests if we limit bot creation in the model. This includes the test in `test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb` (and *maybe* others). However, the benefit of model validation is likely worth it. It is *expected* to fail, which is a good thing (ensuring all tests are updated to take the limit into account).
*   **Browser Tests:** Browser tests cover the happy path and most of the unhappy paths. They do not prevent race conditions, and they do not prevent direct usage of the model.

**Analysis**

This is not a straightforward decision. While it might seem easier to only validate in the controller to avoid potentially breaking tests, that's short-sighted. Given the importance of robustly enforcing the bot limit across *all* possible creation methods, I'm leaning toward implementing *both* model and controller validation. This provides the strongest defense-in-depth approach. We'll need to carefully update our existing tests, and it *will* add some complexity, but the added reliability and maintainability make it the better long-term choice.

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot sets role, generates unique bot_token and bot_key, and does not join open rooms by default" do
    bot = nil
    assert_no_difference -> { Membership.count } do
      bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    end

    assert bot.bot?
    assert bot.active?
    assert_not bot.add_to_all_open_rooms?
    assert_equal users(:kevin), bot.creator
    assert_equal "", bot.password_digest
    assert_nil bot.email_address
    assert_match /\A[A-Za-z0-9]{24}\z/, bot.bot_token
    assert_equal "#{bot.id}-#{bot.bot_token}", bot.bot_key
    assert_empty bot.rooms

    other_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "CI Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not_equal bot.bot_token, other_bot.bot_token
    assert_not_equal bot.bot_key, other_bot.bot_key
  end

  test "creating a bot with add_to_all_open_rooms joins all existing open rooms" do
    bot = nil
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +Rooms::Open.count do
      bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Everyone Bot", creator: users(:kevin), add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    end

    assert bot.add_to_all_open_rooms?
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
  end

  test "toggling add_to_all_open_rooms on joins missing open rooms and toggling off keeps current memberships" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Toggle Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    rooms(:hq).memberships.grant_to(bot)
    rooms(:watercooler).memberships.grant_to(bot)

    assert_equal [ rooms(:hq).id, rooms(:watercooler).id ].sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort

    # Turning on adds missing open rooms without duplicating existing memberships
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +(Rooms::Open.count - 1) do
      bot.update!(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    end
    assert_equal (Rooms::Open.pluck(:id) + [ rooms(:watercooler).id ]).sort, bot.reload.rooms.pluck(:id).sort

    # Turning off keeps all existing memberships
    assert_no_difference -> { Membership.count } do
      bot.update!(add_to_all_open_rooms: false)
    end
    assert_equal (Rooms::Open.pluck(:id) + [ rooms(:watercooler).id ]).sort, bot.reload.rooms.pluck(:id).sort

    # New open rooms created while off do not include the bot
    later_open = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later Open", creator: users(:david))
    assert_not_includes later_open.users, bot

    # Turning back on joins the newly created open room
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +1 do
      bot.update!(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    end
    assert_includes later_open.reload.users, bot
  end

  test "bot name is required" do
    bot = User.new(role: :bot, name: "   ", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin), webhook_url: "  https://bot.example.com/hook  ")
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.webhook.url
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.webhook_url

    original_webhook_id = bot.webhook.id

    # Updating name without webhook_url preserves existing webhook
    bot.update!(name: "Release Bot")
    assert_equal original_webhook_id, bot.reload.webhook.id
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.webhook_url

    # Updating webhook_url updates existing webhook in place
    bot.update!(webhook_url: "http://127.0.0.1:4567/events")
    assert_equal original_webhook_id, bot.reload.webhook.id
    assert_equal "http://127.0.0.1:4567/events", bot.webhook_url

    # Invalid update on name does not delete existing webhook
    assert_not bot.update(name: "", webhook_url: "")
    assert_equal "http://127.0.0.1:4567/events", bot.reload.webhook.url
    assert_equal "http://127.0.0.1:4567/events", bot.webhook_url

    # Blank webhook_url removes the webhook
    bot.update!(webhook_url: "   ")
    assert_nil bot.webhook
    assert_nil bot.webhook_url
    assert_nil bot.reload.webhook
  end

  test "bot rejects invalid webhook_url" do
    bot = User.new(role: :bot, name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin), webhook_url: "ftp://example.com/hook")
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:webhook_url], "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL"
    assert_equal "ftp://example.com/hook", bot.webhook_url
  end

  test "authenticate_bot validates bot_key strictly" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key)

    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("invalid")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-wrongtoken")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}abc-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("999999-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-#{bot.bot_token}-extra")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{users(:david).id}-#{bot.bot_token}")
  end

  test "deactivating a bot revokes its token, removes its webhook and non-direct memberships, preserves messages, and blocks authentication" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin), webhook_url: "https://bot.example.com/hook", add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    old_key = bot.bot_key
    webhook_id = bot.webhook.id
    message = rooms(:hq).messages.create!(body: "Deploy done", creator: bot)

    bot.deactivate
    bot.reload

    assert bot.deactivated?
    assert_nil bot.bot_token
    assert_nil bot.bot_key
    assert_nil bot.webhook
    assert_not Webhook.exists?(webhook_id)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(old_key)
    assert_empty bot.memberships.without_direct_rooms
    assert Message.exists?(message.id)
    assert_equal bot, message.reload.creator
  end

  test "creating a new open room grants membership to people and opt-in active bots only" do
    opt_in_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Opt-In Bot", creator: users(:kevin), add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    manual_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Manual Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    deleted_opt_in_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deleted Bot", creator: users(:kevin), add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    deleted_opt_in_bot.deactivate

    room = Rooms::Open.create_for({ name: "Releases", creator: users(:david) }, users: users(:david))

    assert_includes room.reload.users, opt_in_bot
    assert_not_includes room.users, manual_bot
    assert_not_includes room.users, deleted_opt_in_bot
  end

  test "can_administer? allows creator and administrators but denies other members" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert users(:kevin).can_administer?(bot)
    assert users(:david).can_administer?(bot)
    assert_not users(:jz).can_administer?(bot)
    assert_not bot.can_administer?
    assert_not bot.can_administer?(rooms(:hq))
  end

  test "bot_token is filtered in inspect output" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_not_includes bot.inspect, bot.bot_token
    assert_includes bot.inspect, "[FILTERED]"
  end
end

messages.thinking:
**Transaction Mode and Race Conditions**

Okay, so I was looking at the `config/database.yml` and noticed the `default_transaction_mode: immediate` setting in SQLite. That's interesting! With this configuration, the validations for `User.save` run *inside* an `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction`. I need to be sure about this. I've got to check where the `valid?` method is executed relative to the transaction. Let me trace the execution: `save` calls `perform_validations`, which calls `valid?`, and *then* the `with_transaction_returning_status` is opened! So, unless we explicitly wrap the call in `User.transaction`, validations happen *before* the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction!

That's a potentially huge catch for the race condition. If we wrap `save` in `BotsController#create` or in `User.create_bot!` with `User.transaction`, we get these benefits:
1.  Thread 1 enters `User.transaction` and SQLite executes `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` immediately.
2.  Thread 2 enters `User.transaction` and SQLite waits on `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` until Thread 1 commits.
3.  Thread 1 runs the `creator.at_bot_limit?` check (sees 4 < 5), and inserts bot #5, commits.
4.  Thread 2 acquires the write lock and re-checks the limit and then sees 5 >= 5, so the validation fails/limit check, which rolls back, and returns the 403.

This means we completely eliminate the race condition. Even under heavy load with multiple concurrent `POST /bots` requests, a member will *never* be able to exceed the limit.

Now, what about checking inside `User.transaction` in `BotsController#create` and ALSO in a `before_action :ensure_can_create_bot`? Let's go through the control flow. We can see that the `before_action` handles the check. Also, using a `return` inside `User.transaction` in rails commits the transaction, and it is harmless since nothing was written, and the return then returns out of `create`. Let's avoid that to make things cleaner and to match RuboCop/Rails style. Using `limit_reached = true` is a clean way to ensure the correct behavior. Let's trace it through `BotsController`:

1.  `GET /bots`:
    *   Under limit (or admin): Shows `"Add a chat bot"` link + bot list (or `"No chat bots yet."`).
    *   At/over limit (member): Does *NOT* show `"Add a chat bot"` link, shows `"You’ve reached the limit of N chat bots."` + existing bot list (or `"No chat bots yet."` if limit is 0 and they have 0 bots).
2.  `GET /bots/new`:
    *   Under limit (or admin): `200 OK`, shows `"Add a chat bot"` form.
    *   At/over limit (member): `403 Forbidden`, renders `bots/limit_reached.html.erb` with back link to `/bots`, heading `"Chat bots"`, message `"You’ve reached the limit of N chat bots."`, NO form, NO `"Add a chat bot"`.
3.  `POST /bots`:
    *   Under limit (or admin): validates & saves bot (inside `User.transaction` with `IMMEDIATE` lock).
        *   Valid: `302` redirect to `/bots`.
        *   Invalid (blank name / invalid webhook): `422 Unprocessable Content`, re-renders `:new` with errors.
    *   At/over limit (member): `403 Forbidden`, renders `bots/limit_reached.html.erb`, creates NO bot!
    *   Race condition (two concurrent `POST /bots` when 1 slot remaining): First succeeds (`302`), second hits `limit_reached = true` inside `User.transaction`, returns `403 Forbidden`, creates NO second bot!
4.  `GET /bots/:id/edit`, `PATCH /bots/:id`, `DELETE /bots/:id`:
    *   Even when at or over the limit, member CAN still edit and delete their own existing bots!
5.  Model-level `User.create_bot!` / `User.new(role: :bot, creator: member).save`:
    *   `validate :validate_bot_limit, on: :create, if: :bot?` ALSO enforces the limit at the model layer!

module User::Bot
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true
    has_many :created_bots, -> { bot }, class_name: "User", foreign_key: :creator_id
    has_one :webhook, dependent: :destroy

    before_validation :initialize_bot, on: :create, if: :bot?
    validate :validate_webhook_url, if: :bot?
    validate :validate_bot_limit, on: :create, if: :bot?
    after_save :sync_webhook, if: :bot?

    scope :without_bots, -> { where.not(role: :bot) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def create_bot!(attributes)
      transaction do
        create! attributes.merge(role: :bot)
      end
    end

    def authenticate_bot(bot_key)
      id, token = bot_key.to_s.split("-", 2)
      return nil unless id&.match?(/\A\d+\z/) && token.present?

      if bot = active.bot.find_by(id: id)
        bot if bot.bot_token.present? && ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(bot.bot_token, token)
      end
    end
  end

  def bot_key
    "#{id}-#{bot_token}" if bot? && bot_token.present?
  end

  def at_bot_limit?(account: Current.account)
    return false if administrator? || account.nil?

    created_bots.active.count >= account.settings.bots_per_member
  end

  def can_create_bot?(account: Current.account)
    !at_bot_limit?(account: account)
  end

  def webhook_url
    if defined?(@webhook_url)
      @webhook_url
    else
      webhook&.url
    end
  end

  def webhook_url=(value)
    @webhook_url = value.to_s.strip
  end

  def reload(*)
    remove_instance_variable(:@webhook_url) if defined?(@webhook_url)
    super
  end

  private
    def initialize_bot
      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token
      self.password_digest ||= ""
    end

    def generate_bot_token
      SecureRandom.base58(24)
    end

    def validate_webhook_url
      return unless defined?(@webhook_url) && @webhook_url.present?

      unless Webhook.valid_url?(@webhook_url)
        errors.add :webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL"
      end
    end

    def validate_bot_limit
      return unless active? && creator&.at_bot_limit?

      limit = Current.account.settings.bots_per_member
      errors.add :base, "You’ve reached the limit of #{limit} #{"chat bot".pluralize(limit)}."
    end

    def sync_webhook
      return unless defined?(@webhook_url)

      if @webhook_url.present?
        if webhook
          webhook.update!(url: @webhook_url)
        else
          create_webhook!(url: @webhook_url)
        end
      else
        webhook&.destroy!
        association(:webhook).reset
      end

      remove_instance_variable(:@webhook_url)
    end
end

### Catch #1: Account Settings Overwrite

Okay, let's break this down. The `AccountTest#test_settings` failure is really interesting. **A Moment of Profound Clarity**

Whoa! Look at this HTML form output! It's remarkably clean, semantic, accessible, and idiomatic. I'm especially pleased with how well structured the form elements are. The use of classes like `flex flex-column gap`, along with the semantic HTML elements, makes for an easily understandable and maintainable structure.

But wait a second! This `action="/account.873240054"` in the `<form>` tag... That's directly related to the singular resource definition (`resource :account`). It's Rails's default behavior, and the `.id` is automatically appended as a format when `account_path` is used without an ID, like `form_with model: @account`. It's what was in the original Campfire code!

Now, the real issue becomes apparent when we consider what happens when a `PATCH /account.873240054` request returns an unprocessable entity (`422`) status via `render :edit, status: :unprocessable_content`. When it redirects after a successful update, the redirect is to `/account/edit`, which works on any request format because it just returns the HTTP 302 redirect. However, with `render :edit`, the server's trying to render the same HTML back to the browser but the request format is the key here.

If the request is made to `/account.873240054`, and the controller tries to render the `edit` template with that format, Rails is going to throw an `ActionController::UnknownFormat` or `ActionView::MissingTemplate` exception! The server will look for the format `873240054`!

Thank goodness for this careful examination and the rendered HTML! By simply using `url: account_path` in `<%= form_with model: @account...%>` in `app/views/accounts/edit.html.erb`, we can ensure that the form submits to `/account` (a clean URL) instead of `/account.873240054`. This will make sure that the `render :edit, status: :unprocessable_content` renders the `accounts/edit.html.erb` template correctly and avoids the format mismatch. I also noted that `app/views/accounts/custom_styles/edit.html.erb` explicitly passed `url: account_custom_styles_url` for the exact same reason, so it's a pattern to be considered.

The solution is to update `app/views/accounts/edit.html.erb` to pass `url: account_path` on the form!

path = "test/models/user/bot_test.rb"
content = File.read(path)
addition = <<~"RUBY"

  test "members are capped at account bots_per_member and deleted bots do not count" do
    5.times { |i| User.create_bot!(name: "Bot \#{i + 1}", creator: users(:kevin)) }

    assert users(:kevin).at_bot_limit?
    assert_not users(:kevin).can_create_bot?
    assert_not users(:jz).at_bot_limit?

    sixth = User.new(role: :bot, name: "Bot 6", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not sixth.valid?
    assert_match(/reached the limit/, sixth.errors.full_messages.to_sentence)
    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) do
      User.create_bot!(name: "Bot 6", creator: users(:kevin))
    end

    # Deleting a bot frees a slot
    users(:kevin).created_bots.active.first.deactivate
    assert_not users(:kevin).at_bot_limit?
    assert users(:kevin).can_create_bot?
    replacement = User.create_bot!(name: "Replacement Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert replacement.persisted?
    assert users(:kevin).at_bot_limit?
  end

  test "administrators are not limited by bots_per_member even when set to 0" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(settings: { bots_per_member: 0 })

    assert_not users(:david).at_bot_limit?
    assert users(:david).can_create_bot?
    assert users(:kevin).at_bot_limit?

    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Admin Bot", creator: users(:david))
    assert bot.persisted?
    assert_not users(:david).at_bot_limit?
  end

  test "lowering bots_per_member keeps existing bots active and editable while blocking new ones" do
    bots = 4.times.map { |i| User.create_bot!(name: "Bot \#{i + 1}", creator: users(:kevin)) }

    accounts(:signal).update!(settings: { bots_per_member: 2 })

    assert_equal 4, users(:kevin).created_bots.active.count
    assert bots.all? { |b| b.reload.active? }
    assert users(:kevin).at_bot_limit?

    # Existing bots can still be updated
    bots.first.update!(name: "Renamed Bot")
    assert_equal "Renamed Bot", bots.first.reload.name

    # Creating new bots is blocked until active count drops below 2
    assert_not User.new(role: :bot, name: "Blocked", creator: users(:kevin)).valid?

    bots[0].deactivate # 3 active
    assert users(:kevin).at_bot_limit?

    bots[1].deactivate # 2 active (still at limit)
    assert users(:kevin).at_bot_limit?

    bots[2].deactivate # 1 active (under limit)
    assert_not users(:kevin).at_bot_limit?
    assert User.create_bot!(name: "Allowed", creator: users(:kevin)).persisted?
  end
RUBY

File.write(path, content.sub(/\nend\s*\z/, "\n#{addition}end\n"))
'

    assert find("input#account_settings_restrict_room_creation_to_administrators", visible: :all).checked?

    using_session("Kevin") do
      sign_in "kevin@37signals.com"
      visit edit_account_url
      assert_no_field "Bots per member"
      assert_no_text "Bots per member"

      # Visit /bots and create 1st bot (reaches limit of 1)
      visit bots_url
      assert_link "Add a chat bot"
      assert_no_text "reached the limit"

      click_on "Add a chat bot"
      fill_in "Name the bot", with: "Deploy Bot"
      click_button "Save changes"

      assert_text "Deploy Bot"
      assert_no_link "Add a chat bot"
      assert_no_text "Add a chat bot"
      assert_text "reached the limit"

      # Navigating directly to /bots/new is refused
      visit new_bot_url
      assert_text "reached the limit"
      assert_no_field "Name the bot"
      assert_no_text "Add a chat bot"

      # Deleting the bot via native confirm() dialog restores "Add a chat bot"
      visit bots_url
      click_on "Edit Deploy Bot"
      accept_confirm do
        click_button "Delete this chat bot"
      end

      assert_no_text "Deploy Bot"
      assert_link "Add a chat bot"
      assert_no_text "reached the limit"
    end

    # Admin is not limited even when Bots per member is 0
    visit edit_account_url
    fill_in "Bots per member", with: "0"
    find("input#account_settings_bots_per_member").send_keys(:enter)
    assert_selector ".flash"

    visit bots_url
    assert_link "Add a chat bot"
    click_on "Add a chat bot"
    fill_in "Name the bot", with: "Admin Bot"
    click_button "Save changes"

    assert_text "Admin Bot"
    assert_link "Add a chat bot"
    assert_no_text "reached the limit"
  end

  test "stale /bots/new tab submission is refused once member reaches limit" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(settings: { bots_per_member: 1 })

    sign_in "kevin@37signals.com"
    visit new_bot_url
    fill_in "Name the bot", with: "Second Bot"

    # Reach the limit out-of-band (e.g., from another tab)
    User.create_bot!(name: "First Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    # Submitting the stale form is refused and shows "reached the limit"
    click_button "Save changes"

    assert_text "reached the limit"
    assert_no_field "Name the bot"
    assert_equal 1, users(:kevin).created_bots.active.count
  end
end

require "net/http"
require "json"
require "socket"
require "base64"
require "digest/sha1"
require "open3"

# Minimal WebSocket client for CDP
class SimpleWS
  def initialize(url)
    uri = URI(url)
    @sock = TCPSocket.new(uri.host, uri.port)
    key = Base64.strict_encode64(Random.bytes(16))
    req = "GET #{uri.request_uri} HTTP/1.1\r\n" \
          "Host: #{uri.host}:#{uri.port}\r\n" \
          "Upgrade: websocket\r\n" \
          "Connection: Upgrade\r\n" \
          "Sec-WebSocket-Key: #{key}\r\n" \
          "Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n"
    @sock.write(req)
    loop do
      line = @sock.gets
      break if line.nil? || line == "\r\n"
    end
    @id = 0
  end

  def send_text(str)
    bytes = str.b
    frame = +""
    frame << 0x81
    len = bytes.bytesize
    if len < 126
      frame << (0x80 | len)
    elsif len < 65536
      frame << (0x80 | 126)
      frame << [len].pack("n")
    else
      frame << (0x80 | 127)
      frame << [len].pack("Q>")
    end
    mask = Random.bytes(4)
    frame << mask
    masked = bytes.bytes.each_with_index.map { |b, i| b ^ mask.getbyte(i % 4) }.pack("C*")
    frame << masked
    @sock.write(frame)
  end

  def read_frame
    loop do
      h = @sock.read(2)
      raise "EOF" unless h
      b0, b1 = h.bytes
      opcode = b0 & 0x0f
      masked = (b1 & 0x80) != 0
      len = b1 & 0x7f
      if len == 126
        len = @sock.read(2).unpack1("n")
      elsif len == 127
        len = @sock.read(8).unpack1("Q>")
      end
      mask = masked ? @sock.read(4) : nil
      payload = len > 0 ? @sock.read(len) : ""
      if mask
        payload = payload.bytes.each_with_index.map { |b, i| b ^ mask.getbyte(i % 4) }.pack("C*")
      end
      next if opcode == 0x9 || opcode == 0xa
      return payload.force_encoding("UTF-8")
    end
  end

  def cdp(method, params = {})
    @id += 1
    my_id = @id
    send_text(JSON.generate({ id: my_id, method: method, params: params }))
    loop do
      msg = JSON.parse(read_frame)
      if msg["id"] == my_id
        raise "CDP error for #{method}: #{msg["error"]}" if msg["error"]
        return msg["result"]
      end
    end
  end

  def eval_js(expr)
    res = cdp("Runtime.evaluate", expression: expr, awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true)
    if res["exceptionDetails"]
      raise "JS exception: #{res["exceptionDetails"]}"
    end
    res.dig("result", "value")
  end

  def close
    @sock.close rescue nil
  end
end

  def navigate(ws, url)

    sleep 0.8
  end

  def assert_eq(expected, actual, msg)
    raise "FAIL #{msg}: expected #{expected.inspect}, got #{actual.inspect}" unless expected == actual
    puts "PASS: #{msg}"
  end

  def assert_true(cond, msg)
    raise "FAIL #{msg}" unless cond
    puts "PASS: #{msg}"
  end

  # 1. Sign in as admin
  navigate(ws, "http://127.0.0.1:31337/session/new")
  ws.eval_js(<<~JS)
    document.querySelector('input[name="email_address"]').value = "david@example.com";
    document.querySelector('input[name="password"]').value = "secret123456";
    document.querySelector('button[type="submit"]').click();
  JS
  sleep 1.0

  # 2. Visit /account/edit as admin
  navigate(ws, "http://127.0.0.1:31337/account/edit")
  val = ws.eval_js('document.getElementById("account_settings_bots_per_member").value')
  label_text = ws.eval_js('document.querySelector("label[for=account_settings_bots_per_member]").textContent.trim()')

  assert_eq("Bots per member", label_text, "Exact label text is 'Bots per member'")

    el.value = "2";

    el.dispatchEvent(new Event("change", { bubbles: true }));

  sleep 1.0

  ws.eval_js(<<~JS)
    const el = document.getElementById("account_settings_bots_per_member");

  ws.eval_js(<<~JS)

  sleep 1.0

  assert_eq("3", ws.eval_js('document.getElementById("account_settings_bots_per_member").value'), "Bots per member still 3 after toggling switch")

  # 6. Lower Bots per member to 1 via Enter key
  ws.eval_js(<<~JS)
    const el = document.getElementById("account_settings_bots_per_member");

    el.value = "1";

  JS
  sleep 1.0

  navigate(ws, "http://127.0.0.1:31337/account/edit")
  assert_eq("1", ws.eval_js('document.getElementById("account_settings_bots_per_member").value'), "Bots per member saved as 1 via Enter key")

  # 7. Sign out admin and sign in as member Kevin
  ws.cdp("Network.clearBrowserCookies")
  navigate(ws, "http://127.0.0.1:31337/session/new")
  ws.eval_js(<<~JS)
    document.querySelector('input[name="email_address"]').value = "kevin@example.com";
    document.querySelector('input[name="password"]').value = "secret123456";
    document.querySelector('button[type="submit"]').click();
  JS
  sleep 1.0

  # 8. Member does NOT see Bots per member on /account/edit
  navigate(ws, "http://127.0.0.1:31337/account/edit")
  assert_eq(nil, ws.eval_js('document.getElementById("account_settings_bots_per_member")'), "Member does not see Bots per member input")
  assert_true(!ws.eval_js('document.body.innerText').include?("Bots per member"), "Member does not see Bots per member text")

  assert_true(!body.include?("reached the limit"), "Member under limit does not see reached the limit")

require "net/http"
require "json"
require "socket"
require "base64"
require "digest/sha1"

class SimpleWS
  def initialize(url)
    uri = URI(url)
    @sock = TCPSocket.new(uri.host, uri.port)
    key = Base64.strict_encode64(Random.bytes(16))
    req = "GET #{uri.request_uri} HTTP/1.1\r\n" \
          "Host: #{uri.host}:#{uri.port}\r\n" \
          "Upgrade: websocket\r\n" \
          "Connection: Upgrade\r\n" \
          "Sec-WebSocket-Key: #{key}\r\n" \
          "Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n"
    @sock.write(req)
    loop do
      line = @sock.gets
      break if line.nil? || line == "\r\n"
    end
    @id = 0
  end

  def send_text(str)
    bytes = str.b
    frame = +""
    frame << 0x81
    len = bytes.bytesize
    if len < 126
      frame << (0x80 | len)
    elsif len < 65536
      frame << (0x80 | 126)
      frame << [len].pack("n")
    else
      frame << (0x80 | 127)
      frame << [len].pack("Q>")
    end
    mask = Random.bytes(4)
    frame << mask
    masked = bytes.bytes.each_with_index.map { |b, i| b ^ mask.getbyte(i % 4) }.pack("C*")
    frame << masked
    @sock.write(frame)
  end

  def read_frame
    loop do
      h = @sock.read(2)
      raise "EOF" unless h
      b0, b1 = h.bytes
      opcode = b0 & 0x0f
      masked = (b1 & 0x80) != 0
      len = b1 & 0x7f
      if len == 126
        len = @sock.read(2).unpack1("n")
      elsif len == 127
        len = @sock.read(8).unpack1("Q>")
      end
      mask = masked ? @sock.read(4) : nil
      payload = len > 0 ? @sock.read(len) : ""
      if mask
        payload = payload.bytes.each_with_index.map { |b, i| b ^ mask.getbyte(i % 4) }.pack("C*")
      end
      next if opcode == 0x9 || opcode == 0xa
      return payload.force_encoding("UTF-8")
    end
  end

  def cdp(method, params = {})
    @id += 1
    my_id = @id
    send_text(JSON.generate({ id: my_id, method: method, params: params }))
    loop do
      msg = JSON.parse(read_frame)
      if msg["id"] == my_id
        raise "CDP error for #{method}: #{msg["error"]}" if msg["error"]
        return msg["result"]
      end
    end
  end

  def eval_js(expr)
    res = cdp("Runtime.evaluate", expression: expr, awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true)
    if res["exceptionDetails"]
      raise "JS exception: #{res["exceptionDetails"]}"
    end
    res.dig("result", "value")
  end

  def close
    @sock.close rescue nil
  end
end

require "net/http"
require "json"
require "socket"
require "base64"
require "digest/sha1"

class SimpleWS
  def initialize(url)
    uri = URI(url)
    @sock = TCPSocket.new(uri.host, uri.port)
    key = Base64.strict_encode64(Random.bytes(16))
    req = "GET #{uri.request_uri} HTTP/1.1\r\n" \
          "Host: #{uri.host}:#{uri.port}\r\n" \
          "Upgrade: websocket\r\n" \
          "Connection: Upgrade\r\n" \
          "Sec-WebSocket-Key: #{key}\r\n" \
          "Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n"
    @sock.write(req)
    loop do
      line = @sock.gets
      break if line.nil? || line == "\r\n"
    end
    @id = 0
  end

  def send_text(str)
    bytes = str.b
    frame = "".b
    frame << 0x81
    len = bytes.bytesize
    if len < 126
      frame << (0x80 | len)
    elsif len < 65536
      frame << (0x80 | 126)
      frame << [len].pack("n")
    else
      frame << (0x80 | 127)
      frame << [len].pack("Q>")
    end
    mask = Random.bytes(4)
    frame << mask
    masked = bytes.bytes.each_with_index.map { |b, i| b ^ mask.getbyte(i % 4) }.pack("C*")
    frame << masked
    @sock.write(frame)
  end

  def read_frame
    loop do
      h = @sock.read(2)
      raise "EOF" unless h
      b0, b1 = h.bytes
      opcode = b0 & 0x0f
      masked = (b1 & 0x80) != 0
      len = b1 & 0x7f
      if len == 126
        len = @sock.read(2).unpack1("n")
      elsif len == 127
        len = @sock.read(8).unpack1("Q>")
      end
      mask = masked ? @sock.read(4) : nil
      payload = len > 0 ? @sock.read(len) : "".b
      if mask
        payload = payload.bytes.each_with_index.map { |b, i| b ^ mask.getbyte(i % 4) }.pack("C*")
      end
      next if opcode == 0x9 || opcode == 0xa
      return payload.force_encoding("UTF-8")
    end
  end

  def cdp(method, params = {})
    @id += 1
    my_id = @id
    send_text(JSON.generate({ id: my_id, method: method, params: params }))
    loop do
      msg = JSON.parse(read_frame)
      if msg["id"] == my_id
        raise "CDP error for #{method}: #{msg["error"]}" if msg["error"]
        return msg["result"]
      end
    end
  end

    if res["exceptionDetails"]
      raise "JS exception: #{res["exceptionDetails"]}"
    end
    res.dig("result", "value")
  end

  def close
    @sock.close rescue nil
  end

  - `User::Bot` additionally validates `validate_bot_limit` on `:create` (and wraps `User.create_bot!` in a transaction) so model-level creation obeys the same rule.
